steps.detail: Create is_deceased = DOD not null; parse DOD as a date and drop the raw date after deriving the flag
steps.reason: Missing means the beneficiary is alive (99% missing by design), so imputing a date would be wrong.

steps.detail: Parse to date and derive beneficiary age at claim date
steps.reason: Age is more useful than a raw date string.

steps.detail: Parse in inpatient and outpatient; derive claim duration and month
steps.reason: Dates are strings, and claims span Nov 2008 to Dec 2009, so a time-based split is needed for validation.

steps.detail: Parse in inpatient and outpatient; ClaimEndDt minus ClaimStartDt gives duration
steps.reason: Dates are strings; needed for duration features.

steps.detail: Parse the inpatient admission date; derive length of stay with DischargeDt
steps.reason: Dates are strings; needed for stay features.

steps.detail: Parse the inpatient discharge date
steps.reason: Dates are strings; needed for length of stay.

steps.detail: Inpatient: missing -> 0 plus a missing indicator; a single value of 1068 is present otherwise
steps.reason: Only one distinct value exists besides the 2.2% missing, which probably means no deductible was paid. Keep the indicator so the signal is not lost.

steps.detail: Create has_operating_physician flag; leave the ID itself unimputed
steps.reason: Missing by design (41% inpatient, 82% outpatient) because many claims have no operating physician.

steps.detail: Create has_other_physician flag; leave the ID itself unimputed
steps.reason: Missing by design (88% inpatient, 62% outpatient).

steps.detail: Create a missing flag (0.3% missing); do not impute the ID
steps.reason: A missing physician is itself possibly informative; the share is tiny.

steps.detail: Inpatient: create has_procedure flag and procedure count across codes 1-6; keep codes as categorical, not float
steps.reason: Missing means no procedure was performed; the codes are identifiers, not numbers.

steps.detail: Fold into procedure count; do not impute
steps.reason: Missing means no additional procedure (86.5% missing).

steps.detail: Fold into procedure count; do not impute
steps.reason: Missing by design (97.6% missing).

steps.detail: Inpatient: drop after counting; 99.7% missing
steps.reason: Too sparse to carry its own signal; counted in the procedure count first.

steps.detail: Drop in inpatient and outpatient
steps.reason: Essentially empty (~100% missing, at most 6 values), so no usable signal.

steps.detail: Drop in inpatient and outpatient
steps.reason: 100% missing, constant.

steps.detail: Outpatient: 2% missing; flag it and keep codes as categorical. Derive a diagnosis count across codes 1-10 for both claim types
steps.reason: Missing means no diagnosis was recorded; the count is a stronger signal than the sparse later codes.

steps.detail: Drop in inpatient and outpatient after counting
steps.reason: 90-99.8% missing; its content is captured by the diagnosis count.

steps.detail: Outpatient: 79.7% missing, so create a has_admit_dx flag; keep the code as categorical for inpatient
steps.reason: Missing by design, since admit diagnoses mostly belong to inpatient stays.

steps.detail: Join key. Aggregate inpatient and outpatient claims to provider level (claim counts, reimbursement sums and means, distinct beneficiaries, physician counts) and join the labels on it; do not use raw IDs as features
steps.reason: The unit of modelling is the provider, so claim-level data must be rolled up. 5,410 labelled providers; some have no inpatient claims, so fill their inpatient aggregates with 0 plus an indicator.

steps.detail: Join claims to beneficiary attributes; use it only as a key and to count distinct patients per provider
steps.reason: Identifier, not a predictor.

steps.reason: Unique identifier with no signal.
